definition: Version space learning is a logical approach to machine learning, specifically binary classification.
details: Version space learning algorithms search a predefined space of hypotheses, viewed as a set of logical sentences. Formally, the hypothesis space is a disjunction H 1 ∨ H 2 ∨ . . . ∨ H n {\displaystyle H_{1}\lor H_{2}\lor ...\lor H_{n}} (i.e., one or more of hypotheses 1 through n are true). A version space learning algorithm is presented with examples, which it will use to restrict its hypothesis space; for each example x, the hypotheses that are inconsistent with x are removed from the space. This iterative refining of the hypothesis space is called the candidate elimination algorithm, the hypothesis space maintained inside the algorithm, its version space.

explainer.lead: Version space learning is a logical approach to binary classification that narrows a hypothesis space as examples arrive. It matters as a formal, logic-based view of learning from examples.

tiers.eli5: You keep a list of every rule still consistent with what you've seen, and each new example crosses out the rules that no longer fit.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to maintain the set of hypotheses consistent with observed examples. A pitfall is that the version space can stay large or empty, limiting decisive predictions.
tiers.paperLevel: The hypothesis space is the disjunction H1 or H2 ... or Hn; for each example x, hypotheses inconsistent with x are removed. Learning is restricted to the predefined hypothesis space.

explainer.example: After seeing several labeled examples, the algorithm discards every hypothesis that misclassifies them, leaving only consistent ones.
